## FAQ

1. Rutile vs. Anatase --what's the difference?
:   Rutile offers better opacity, brightness, and weather resistance -- ideal for outdoor use. Anatase is more reactive, used for indoor or photocatalytic applications.

2. What specs matter most?
:   TiO2 content (93-96%), particle size (0.2-0.3um), brightness (95min), oil absorption (16-18), and surface treatment type.

3. Sulfate vs. Chloride process -- which is better?
:   Chloride process yields higher purity and better color consistency, with lower environmental impact - preferred for premium grades. Sulfate process is more common in China and cost -effective for general use.

4. How to choose the right grade?
:   Coatings --- rutile + surface treatment; Plastics --- good dispersibility; Inks --- fine particle size; Cosmetics/Food --- FDA-compliant grades.

5. What certifications should a supplier have?
:   ISO 9001, ISO 14001, REACH (for EU), FDA (for food/cosmetic grades), and third-party lab test reports.

6. Is TiO2 safe?
:   Low toxicity for skin contact and ingestion. Inhalation of dust is a concern -- use respiratory protection when handling powder.

7. Why is it expensive?
:   High refractive index (2.73), energy-intensive production, and rising raw material & compliance costs.

8. How to store?
:   Cool, dry, sealed containers. Protect from moisture to prevent caking.

9. Free samples?
:   Yes -- most suppliers offer 0.5--1kg free samples to qualified buyers. Always test in your formulation first.

# Introducing versatile LOMON®R-996 pigment for durable glossy coatings and inks, a high performance TiO2 pigment from Lomon Billions

#### Media Contact

**Julie Reid,** Marketing Director: LB Group, Winder House, Kingfisher Way, Stockton-on-Tees, TS18 3EX, UK

**T**[+44 (0)1642 692750](tel:4401642692750)/**E**[juliereid@lomonbillions.global](mailto:juliereid@lomonbillions.global)

[All News](https://www.lomonbillions.global/press-and-pr/)

[Prev](https://www.lomonbillions.global/lomon-billions-will-promote-its-specialist-high-performance-billionstr52-titanium-dioxide-pigment-for-printing-inks-at-ecs-2017/)

[Next](https://www.lomonbillions.global/billionsblr-895-pigment-is-a-new-high-performance-chloride-titanium-dioxide-pigment-for-coatings-manufactured-by-lomon-billions-and-developed-in-consultation-with-customers/)

#### Visit us at ECS 2017 in Hall 7, stand 7-423 to find out more

**Stockton-On-Tees, UK, 8 th March 2017**: Lomon Billions will promote its versatile LOMON®R-996 titanium dioxide pigment at the European coatings show in Nürnberg, Germany in April, one of its wide range of high performance TiO 2 pigments, manufactured using the sulfate process and designed for use in durable glossy coatings and inks.

_“LOMON®R-996 pigment is a high performance titanium dioxide pigment manufactured using the sulfate process,”_ says Julie Reid, marketing director. _“It’s a rutile pigment with a zirconia and alumina surface treatment and has been designed for use in both water-based and solvent-based formulations. It’s such a versatile pigment – our customers use R-996 pigment to make a wide range of durable, glossy interior and exterior decorative and industrial coatings. It’s also really effective in powder coatings, inks and plastics.”_

Lomon Billions is now the world’s 4 th largest producer of high performance titanium dioxide pigments and 1 st in Asia in terms of TiO 2 pigment production capacity. We manufacture a wide range of high performance titanium dioxide pigments for all major applications using the sulfate process including BILLIONS®TR52 specialist pigment for high quality inks. We also produce TiO 2 pigments using the chloride process including our new versatile BILLIONS®BLR-895 pigment designed for an extensive range of architectural and industrial coatings, and new BILLIONS®BLR-896 pigment, a super-durable TiO 2 pigment designed for use in heavy-duty industrial coatings that are constantly exposed to intense weathering. Our focus on reliability, innovation and technical excellence delivers product consistency and customer satisfaction.

Lomon Billions is a dynamic, global business with a strong and expanding European presence and is investing in the future. We’ve been manufacturing TiO 2 pigments for over 25 years. We have three established ISO certified production sites with a total annual production capacity of over 600,000 tons and plans to significantly grow production capacity.

We’re exhibiting ECS 2017 in Nürnberg, Germany from 4-6 April.

 Visit us in Hall 7, stand 7-423 to find out more about the benefits we can deliver.

 Contact Julie Reid at [juliereid@billionseurope.com](mailto:juliereid@billionseurope.com) to make an appointment, or visit our website [www.lomonbillions.com](http://www.billionsglobal.com/).

Ends

Henan Billions Chemicals Company Ltd merged with Lomon* to form Lomon Billions on October 28**th**, 2016. The company’s headquarters is in Jiaozuo, Henan Province, China. Its European headquarters is in Stockton On Tees, UK, and its headquarters in the USA is in Chicago Illinois. Lomon Billions has three established ISO certified TiO 2 pigment production sites in China in Jiaozuo, Henan Province, Deyang, Sichuan Province and Xiangyang, Hubei Province, and an ilmenite mine in Panzhihua, Sichuan Province. It is the only company in China that manufactures titanium dioxide pigment using both the chloride and sulfate process. The merged company has a total annual production capacity of over 600,000 tons and is ranked 4**th**in the world and 1**st**in Asia in terms of TiO**2**pigment production capacity. In 2015 the combined TiO**2**pigment sales volume of Henan Billions and Lomon was 560,000 tons: 310,000 tons domestic and 250,000 tons export, with the export volume representing around 50% of the total TiO**2**pigment export volume from China. This $1.47billion merger broke the record for capital refinancing in Henan Province and created a company listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange with a market value of over 30 billion RMB ($4.36 billion).

_*Sichuan Lomon Titanium Industry Co., Ltd_
